$comment: linux-arm64 and win32-arm64 are pinned but their checksums are not recorded yet: nobody has downloaded
those two archives to hash them, and neither is in the release matrix. Run --record on them before
adding either to `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml`.
ffmpeg, pinned per platform. It ships inside the installer, unlike yt-dlp (ADR 0010). ffprobe does not:
the app reads durations from the headers of the WAVs it writes (`wavDurationMs` in server/lib/audio.ts).
The Dockerfile fetches `latest` and that is fine for a self-hoster building an image on their own
machine; it is not fine for a binary you sign and hand to other people, so every entry here names
one immutable build and the SHA-256 its archive must have. A mismatch fails the fetch.
What a build has to carry: libmp3lame for the MP3 export, the decoders for every upload format and
the AAC/Opus yt-dlp downloads, and the reverb, low-pass, and mixing filters. It no longer needs
librubberband: the Mix render stretches with Rubber Band WebAssembly, not ffmpeg's rubberband filter
(ADR 0003 and ADR 0004 amendments). Windows and Linux are still BtbN's `gpl` variant from before
that; whether a slimmer build would do is `.scratch/apple-silicon-release/issues/05-slimmer-bundled-ffmpeg.md`.
Every archive the release matrix fetches is mirrored as an asset on this repo's own `bundled-ffmpeg-*`
prerelease, and `url` points there; `$upstream` records where it came from. A third party's retention
is not ours to rely on: BtbN deletes its daily autobuilds after about two weeks, and the 1.3.0 release
failed on a pin that had been pruned. To move a pin, download the new upstream archive, --record it,
cross-check the publisher's checksum, and upload it to a new mirror release; never edit an existing one.
A null sha256 means nobody has verified that build yet, and `fetch-binaries.ts` refuses it. Run it
with --record on a machine that can reach the URL to fill one in.

win32-x64.$verified: Downloaded, matched against BtbN's checksums.sha256, extracted, and run: `ffmpeg -encoders` lists libmp3lame.

linux-x64.$verified: Downloaded, hashed, and matched against BtbN's checksums.sha256. Not run — the machine that pinned it was Windows. Same BtbN build and `gpl` variant as win32-x64, which was run.

darwin-arm64.$comment: Apple Silicon only; there is no Intel macOS build. martin-riedl.de's 9.0.1 release build, which ships each binary as its own zip under a versioned, timestamped path; only ffmpeg.zip is fetched. It has no librubberband, and the render no longer needs it.
darwin-arm64.$verified: Downloaded on Windows and inspected rather than run. Both archives match the SHA-256 the publisher lists beside them. Both binaries are thin arm64 Mach-O, not universal, and every library they load is under /usr/lib or /System/Library, so nothing outside macOS itself. The configuration is --enable-gpl --enable-version3 --enable-libmp3lame, and codecs.txt lists the libmp3lame encoder and the aac, mp3, flac, opus, and vorbis decoders. The release workflow's macOS leg re-checks the architecture, libraries, and encoder on the runner before building.
